hypotheses.justification: The statement does not need s-finiteness to elaborate: `μ.prod ν` is defined for any `ν` (it takes the junk value 0 if `ν` is not s-finite, see Measure.prod in Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Prod.lean). The proof uses it only through `Measure.measure_prod_null htmeas`, and only in the direction `(fun x => ν (Prod.mk x ⁻¹' t)) =ᵐ[μ] 0 → μ.prod ν t = 0`. Mathlib has `Measure.measure_prod_null_of_ae_null` (hsm : MeasurableSet s) (hs : (fun x => ν (Prod.mk x ⁻¹' s)) =ᵐ[μ] 0) : μ.prod ν s = 0, which is stated `omit [SFinite ν]` and relies on `prod_apply_le`, which also needs no s-finiteness. So the proof of the theorem goes through without the hypothesis. First take the measurable `t ⊆ s \ G` that is a.e.-equal to `s \ G`, as in the existing proof. Then, for each `x`, show `ν (Prod.mk x ⁻¹' t) = 0` by the same section argument, which uses no s-finiteness. Conclude `μ.prod ν t = 0` with `measure_prod_null_of_ae_null htmeas` applied to `Filter.Eventually.of_forall` of that fact, and finish with `measure_congr`. The other hypotheses (`hs`, `hbad`, `hsection`) are still used. The only dependence on `[SFinite ν]` is in the helper `prod_measure_diff_eq_zero_of_ae_ae_restrict_section₀`, which would have to be reproved or generalized in the same way.
